messages.subject: CODEX k=17 returning significantly more CNV
parts:
Hi Xiao,

 

Did you choose the optimal K=16 by one chromosome? There are cases (certain K values at certain chromosomes) where the parameter estimation doesn’t converge. I strongly suspect this is the case for chr7 K=16. I would suggest once you pick an optimal K from one chromosome, rerun the entire genome with a restricted space of potential K values (for this study, for example, normalize using K=15:19).

 

I am glad CODEX is performing well! I am cc’ing CODEX’s user group so other users can see this thread if they have similar questions.

 

Cheers,

Yuchao

 

From: jixiao2...@gmail.com [mailto:jixiao2...@gmail.com] On Behalf Of Xiao Ji
Sent: Friday, May 01, 2015 3:44 PM
To: Yuchao Jiang
Subject: CODEX potential bug

 

Hi Yuchao,

 

I re-ran CODEX on my data and found something unusual. This time I used normalize1 for my case/control data on all chromosomes. 

 

When # latent factors=16, it returned 254279 CNV calls from chr7, which is unusually high (even higher than the sum of all of the rest of chromosomes.) However the other chromosomes looks fine.  I compared them with my earlier norm2 run, the chr7 looked normal there.

 

I tried # latent factors=17, it returned 15926 CNV calls from chr7, which should be normal.

 

Do you know the possible reason for this problem? (I attached the CNV call results with #latent=16 & #latent=17)

 

BTW, the norm1 run on my trios data looks fine. The performance is indeed higher than that of the intersect of CODEX & XHMM. So my conclusion is that normalization should be done on both cases and controls at least in the setting of WES on normal tissues.

 

best,

Xiao
